items.prompt: An ANALYST sends PATCH /api/workflows/:id with a body that would also fail schema validation. Which status comes back?
items.answer: 403 FORBIDDEN, because the permission check runs first
distractors: 500, as the ZodError from the body is caught as unknown
400 with the list of field errors from the schema parse
404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as analysts see no workflows
items.explanation: executeRoute asserts the route permission before it parses the body, and workflow:write is not in the analyst matrix, so the AppError(403) is thrown first.

items.prompt: Operator B manually triggers an ACTIVE workflow that operator A created. What does the dispatch service return?
items.answer: 404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as operators only see their own
distractors: 403 WORKFLOW_SCOPE_VIOLATION from the ownership check itself
201, as any operator may trigger an active workflow
409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE for another owner's workflow
items.explanation: findById applies the "own" visibility scope for operators, so the workflow is not found and the 404 is thrown before assertCanManageWorkflow is ever reached.

items.prompt: An operator manually triggers their own workflow while it is PAUSED. What is the response?
items.answer: 409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE; only ACTIVE ones can run
distractors: 201, as a manual trigger also works when paused
422, as paused workflows must be republished first
403, as a paused workflow is locked to admins
items.explanation: After the scoped load and the ownership check, triggerWorkflowManually throws 409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE for any status other than ACTIVE.

items.prompt: An operator manually triggers their own ACTIVE workflow whose trigger type is SCHEDULE. What happens?
items.answer: A run is queued with triggerSource "manual" and 201
distractors: 409, since scheduled workflows are started by cron alone
422, since a manual run needs an event name to be set
A run is queued, and nextScheduledAt moves ahead
items.explanation: triggerWorkflowManually checks only that the workflow is ACTIVE; it never looks at triggerType. It enqueues with source "manual" and does not touch nextScheduledAt.

items.prompt: A step has maxRetries 2 and its HTTP action throws every time. How often does it run, and what waits come between the attempts?
items.answer: Three attempts, with waits of 15 s and then 30 s
distractors: Two attempts, with one wait of 15 s in between
Four attempts, waiting 15 s, 30 s and then 45 s
Two retries after the first try, each after 30 s
items.explanation: The job's maxAttempts is maxRetries + 1 = 3. On failure readyAt is now + attempts * 15 000 ms, so 15 s after the first failure and 30 s after the second; the third failure marks the step failed and the job dead.

items.prompt: A worker leases a job and then its process is killed. The lease was for 30 seconds. What happens to the job afterwards?
items.answer: It stays LEASED, as leasing only takes AVAILABLE rows
distractors: After 30 s another worker leases it again under a new token
It is reset to AVAILABLE by the scheduler on its next tick
It is marked dead once leasedUntil has passed without work
items.explanation: leaseNextAvailableJob selects status = 'AVAILABLE' AND readyAt <= NOW(); nothing turns an expired LEASED row back into AVAILABLE, so the run stays RUNNING.

items.prompt: An hourly SCHEDULE workflow was due at 01:00, 02:00 and 03:00, but the scheduler was down until 03:30. What happens on its first tick?
items.answer: One run is created, and the next time is set from 03:30
distractors: Three runs are created, one for each missed interval
No run is created; the missed ticks are simply skipped
Three runs are created and the next time is 04:00
items.explanation: dispatchScheduledRuns enqueues once per due workflow, then sets nextScheduledAt with getNextScheduledAt(cron, now), so missed ticks collapse into one catch-up run.

items.prompt: An operator saves a workflow whose step name is one character long, below the schema's min(2). What does the API return?
distractors: 400, with each of the zod field errors in the response
422 with a WORKFLOW_STEP_REQUIRED code
201, as step names are not validated yet
items.explanation: bodySchema.parse throws a ZodError, which is not an AppError, so executeRoute's catch returns the generic 500, without logging it.

items.prompt: A step condition says context.riskScore lt 50, but no earlier step ever wrote riskScore. Does the step run?
items.answer: Yes: the missing value reads as null, and Number(null) is 0
distractors: No: a missing path makes every comparison in the rule false
No: a missing value is NaN, and NaN is never below 50
Yes: conditions are skipped for keys that are not present
items.explanation: readPath returns null for a missing segment; lt compares Number(null) < Number(50), which is 0 < 50, so the rule matches and the step runs.

items.prompt: A step's HTTP URL is "https://api.test/orders/{{payload.orderId}}", but the trigger payload has no orderId. What URL is called?
items.answer: "https://api.test/orders/" with the token replaced by an empty string
distractors: The URL unchanged, with the literal {{payload.orderId}} placeholder
"https://api.test/orders/undefined", since the lookup returns undefined
None: the step throws a missing-variable error and enters retrying
items.explanation: lookupToken returns "" for a segment that is not present, and resolveTemplateStrings substitutes String(""), so the placeholder disappears and the request goes to /orders/.

items.prompt: An operator tries to move their PAUSED workflow back to DRAFT. What does assertValidWorkflowTransition do?
distractors: Allows it, as PAUSED may return to any earlier status
Allows it only when no runs have been created so far
Throws 422, as DRAFT is not a valid target status
items.explanation: allowedTransitions lists PAUSED: [ACTIVE, ARCHIVED]. A same-state request returns early, but PAUSED to DRAFT is not allowed and throws 409.

items.prompt: An ANALYST and an OPERATOR who created no workflows both call GET /api/workflows. What do they each see?
items.answer: The analyst sees every workflow; the operator sees none
distractors: Both see every workflow, as reads are open to all
Neither sees any, as both of them created nothing
The operator sees every workflow; the analyst sees shared ones
items.explanation: getWorkflowVisibilityScope returns "all" for ADMIN and ANALYST and "own" for OPERATOR, so a read-only analyst sees more than an operator does.

items.front: In what order does executeRoute handle a request, and how are errors mapped?
items.back: Load the session actor; if the route needs a permission, 401 without an actor, then assertPermission (403); then parse the body; then run the handler. AppError keeps its status; anything else (ZodError, SyntaxError, Prisma errors) becomes a generic 500 and is not logged.

items.front: How does a failed step get retried in FlowForge?
items.back: In the worker catch: attempts = job.attempts + 1. If attempts < maxAttempts (maxRetries + 1), markStepRetrying resets the same job row to AVAILABLE with readyAt = now + attempts * 15 s and the step to RETRYING, in one transaction. Otherwise the step is marked failed and the job dead.

items.front: Why can a run stay RUNNING forever, and what is the fix?
items.back: The lease query only takes AVAILABLE rows, so a job leased by a worker that died stays LEASED. Fix: also select LEASED rows whose leasedUntil < NOW(), and check leaseToken when completing so a slow worker cannot finish a job re-leased to someone else.

items.front: How can one scheduled tick produce two runs?
items.back: The scheduler loop and the internal dispatch route can run dispatchScheduledRuns concurrently; it reads due workflows, enqueues, then advances nextScheduledAt with no lock. Fix: claim with a conditional update on nextScheduledAt and enqueue only if one row changed.
